stem: A 76-year-old started oxybutynin 3 weeks ago. Her family reports dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and new forgetfulness. What links all four?

options.A: CYP2D6 inhibition of her other drugs
options.B: Beta3 stimulation of the detrusor
options.C: Systemic antimuscarinic blockade
options.D: PDE5 inhibition and cGMP build-up
options.E: Alpha1 blockade in vessels and the iris

why: Antimuscarinic adverse effects follow from systemic blockade: dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and, importantly, cognitive impairment and confusion in older adults.

whys.A: That is the mirabegron interaction.
whys.D: That is sildenafil and tadalafil.

takeaway: Dry, constipated, blurry, confused: antimuscarinic.
discriminator: One mechanism explains the whole list.

stem: A 26-year-old has used DMPA injections for 4 years and wants to continue long term. She has irregular spotting and asks about any lasting risks. Which point should be covered?

options.A: Venous thromboembolism risk equal to a combined pill
options.B: Permanent infertility after more than 2 years of use
options.C: Endometrial cancer risk from unopposed progestin exposure
options.D: Erythrocytosis, so hematocrit is monitored each year
options.E: Bone mineral density loss with prolonged use, which is reversible

why: Progestin-only methods cause irregular bleeding, especially early, and mood changes. DMPA specifically causes reversible bone mineral density loss with prolonged use.

whys.A: VTE is the estrogen concern.
whys.B: This is not a taught DMPA effect.
whys.C: The endometrial risk is from unopposed estrogen.
whys.D: That is testosterone therapy.

takeaway: DMPA long term: think bone density.
discriminator: Class effect (spotting) vs DMPA-specific effect (bone).

stem: A 67-year-old with stable angina takes isosorbide mononitrate daily and asks for sildenafil. Which response matches the lecture?

options.A: Do not prescribe; involve his cardiologist about the nitrate first
options.B: Stop the nitrate yourself today and start sildenafil
options.C: Prescribe sildenafil at half dose with close monitoring
options.D: Prescribe sildenafil and space it 4 hours from the nitrate
options.E: Prescribe tadalafil instead, which is safe with nitrates

why: Nitrates raise NO and cGMP; PDE5 inhibitors stop cGMP breakdown. Together: profound hypotension and syncope. It is an absolute contraindication, and ED treatment decisions involve the cardiologist.

whys.B: Any change to anginal therapy involves his cardiologist.
whys.C: No dose makes the combination acceptable.
whys.D: Spacing is for alpha1 blockers; nitrates are an absolute contraindication.
whys.E: The whole class is contraindicated with nitrates.

takeaway: Nitrate on board: no PDE5 inhibitor.
discriminator: Absolute with nitrates; caution with alpha1 blockers.

stem: A 64-year-old with blood pressure 168/102 despite two drugs is offered mirabegron for overactive bladder. He also takes a drug cleared by CYP2D6. Which two cautions apply?

options.A: It causes confusion, and it is opposed by donepezil
options.B: It halves PSA, and it lowers libido over months
options.C: It is raised by CYP3A4 inhibitors, like solifenacin is
options.D: It can raise blood pressure, and it inhibits CYP2D6
options.E: It causes first-dose hypotension and floppy iris syndrome

why: Mirabegron can raise blood pressure (monitor in uncontrolled hypertension) and inhibits CYP2D6.

whys.A: Those are antimuscarinic issues.
whys.C: The taught mirabegron interaction is its own CYP2D6 inhibition.

takeaway: Mirabegron: check the blood pressure and the CYP2D6 list.
discriminator: Beta3 agonist cautions vs antimuscarinic cautions.

stem: A 58-year-old has taken tamoxifen for 3 years after breast cancer. She mentions light vaginal spotting for 2 weeks and wonders whether to wait until her next annual visit. What is the best response?

options.A: Check hematocrit and PSA, then review in 6 months
options.B: Add estradiol alone to stabilize the uterine lining
options.C: Arrange prompt gynecologic evaluation for endometrial disease
options.D: Switch to raloxifene, which treats the endometrium
options.E: Reassure her; spotting is expected and needs no workup

why: Tamoxifen is an antagonist in breast but an agonist in endometrium, raising the risk of hyperplasia and cancer. Abnormal bleeding needs prompt gynecologic evaluation.

whys.A: Those are testosterone monitoring items.
whys.D: Raloxifene is endometrium-neutral; the bleeding still needs evaluation.
whys.E: Bleeding on tamoxifen should not be dismissed.

takeaway: Bleeding on tamoxifen: evaluate now.
discriminator: Same drug, opposite action in two tissues.

stem: A 62-year-old takes tamsulosin for BPH and wants to start tadalafil for erectile dysfunction. He takes no nitrates. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Absolutely contraindicated, exactly as with nitrates
options.B: Tadalafil raises tamsulosin levels through CYP2D6
options.C: Tamsulosin blocks tadalafil's effect on cGMP entirely
options.D: Additive hypotension: space the doses or monitor closely
options.E: No interaction, because the two act on different tissues

why: Alpha1 blockers and PDE5 inhibitors together cause additive hypotension: less severe than with nitrates, but it warrants spacing doses or careful monitoring.

whys.A: The alpha1-blocker interaction is less severe.
whys.C: They add to each other's hypotension.

takeaway: Alpha1 blocker + PDE5 inhibitor: caution, not a ban.
discriminator: Nitrates: never. Alpha1 blockers: carefully.

stem: A 23-year-old started a progestin-only pill 6 weeks ago and has unpredictable spotting. She is worried something is wrong. What is the best counseling?

options.A: Spotting signals endometrial cancer from the progestin
options.B: Irregular bleeding is common early with progestin-only methods
options.C: Spotting signals enzyme induction by the pill itself
options.D: Spotting signals a clot; stop the pill immediately
options.E: Spotting signals bone loss, as with every progestin

why: Progestin-only methods have more irregular bleeding patterns, especially initially.

whys.A: That risk is from unopposed estrogen or tamoxifen.
whys.C: Induction comes from other drugs.
whys.D: VTE is the estrogen concern.
whys.E: Bone loss is specific to prolonged DMPA.

takeaway: Progestin-only: early spotting is expected.
discriminator: Expected nuisance vs warning sign.

stem: A 29-year-old with PCOS starts metformin. After 5 days she has nausea and loose stools and wants to stop. Her renal function is normal. What is the best advice?

options.A: A sign of B12 deficiency; check a level this week
options.B: An allergy; switch to a sulfonylurea to avoid GI effects
options.C: Common and often transient; take it with meals
options.D: A sign of lactic acidosis; stop it and go to the hospital
options.E: Expected; take it on an empty stomach to absorb it better

why: Metformin's common early effect is GI upset (nausea, diarrhea), often transient; take with meals. Lactic acidosis is rare but serious and linked to renal impairment.

whys.A: B12 deficiency follows long-term use.
whys.B: This is an expected effect, not an allergy.
whys.D: Lactic acidosis is rare and tied to renal impairment.

takeaway: Early metformin GI upset: with meals, and wait.
discriminator: Common and early vs rare and renal.

stem: A 59-year-old on sildenafil starts ketoconazole. After his next dose he has a pounding headache, marked flushing and a blue tint to his vision. What explains the stronger effects?

options.A: Ketoconazole blocks alpha1 receptors in vessel walls
options.B: Ketoconazole induces CYP3A4 and lowers sildenafil levels
options.C: Ketoconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and raises sildenafil levels
options.D: The blue vision shows an allergy unrelated to dose
options.E: Ketoconazole donates NO and raises cGMP like a nitrate

why: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin) raise PDE5 inhibitor levels. Headache, flushing, dyspepsia and blue-tinged vision are the class adverse effects, more notable with sildenafil.

whys.A: That is tamsulosin.
whys.B: Lower levels would weaken the effects.
whys.D: Visual change is a known, dose-related PDE5 effect.

takeaway: CYP3A4 inhibitor + PDE5 inhibitor = exaggerated effects.
discriminator: Expected adverse effects, at a higher level.

stem: A 44-year-old premenopausal woman with estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer asks why she was not given anastrozole alone like her 68-year-old aunt. Which explanation is correct?

options.A: Aromatase inhibitors only work when the uterus is absent
options.B: Her ovaries still make estrogen, so it is not enough alone
options.C: Aromatase inhibitors need CYP2D6, which falls after menopause
options.D: Her bones are too strong for an aromatase inhibitor to act
options.E: Aromatase inhibitors raise endometrial cancer risk before menopause

why: Aromatase inhibitors block peripheral estrogen synthesis. Before menopause the ovary still makes estrogen, so an aromatase inhibitor alone is insufficient.

whys.A: The issue is ovarian estrogen, not the uterus.
whys.C: CYP2D6 activation is the tamoxifen story.
whys.D: Bone loss is an adverse effect, not a requirement.

takeaway: Aromatase inhibitors alone are for after menopause.
discriminator: Peripheral synthesis vs ovarian synthesis.

stem: A 31-year-old man using testosterone from a gym contact has been trying to conceive for a year. Semen analysis shows a very low sperm count. What is the mechanism?

options.A: Testosterone causes erythrocytosis that blocks the ducts
options.B: Testosterone blocks 5-alpha-reductase in the testis
options.C: Exogenous testosterone suppresses the testis's own function
options.D: Testosterone raises prolactin by blocking dopamine
options.E: Testosterone is converted to DHT, which destroys sperm

why: Testosterone causes erythrocytosis, hepatotoxicity with oral forms, and suppression of endogenous testicular function and fertility.

whys.A: Erythrocytosis is real but unrelated to fertility.
whys.D: That is antipsychotics and metoclopramide.
whys.E: The taught effect is suppression of endogenous function.

takeaway: Testosterone lowers fertility.
discriminator: Giving the end hormone switches off its own axis.

stem: A 27-year-old with PCOS takes spironolactone for hirsutism. She is started on lisinopril for hypertension. Which monitoring matters most?

options.A: Hematocrit, because both drugs raise it
options.B: Bone density, because both drugs lower it
options.C: INR, because both drugs raise it
options.D: PSA, because both drugs lower it
options.E: Potassium, because both drugs raise it

why: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and potassium cause hyperkalemia with spironolactone.

whys.A: Hematocrit is the testosterone concern.
whys.B: Bone loss is aromatase inhibitors and DMPA.
whys.C: INR rises with tamoxifen or testosterone plus warfarin.
whys.D: PSA is the 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor issue.

takeaway: Spironolactone + ACE inhibitor: potassium.
discriminator: A Unit 5 interaction in a Unit 6 patient.

stem: A 68-year-old has taken dutasteride for 3 years. His PSA was 3.0 ng/mL before treatment and is 2.6 ng/mL now. How should the PA interpret this?

options.A: Reassuring: the PSA has fallen from 3.0 to 2.6
options.B: Concerning: on a 5-ARI a PSA of 2.6 reads as about 5.2
options.C: Concerning: on a 5-ARI a PSA of 2.6 reads as about 1.3
options.D: Reassuring: 5-ARIs do not change PSA values
options.E: Uninterpretable: PSA cannot be used on dutasteride

why: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors lower PSA by roughly half with long-term therapy, so the value is read accordingly. A PSA that has barely fallen is effectively higher than baseline.

whys.A: It should have fallen by about half.
whys.C: The correction is to double, not halve.
whys.D: They lower PSA by roughly half.
whys.E: It can be used once adjusted.

takeaway: On finasteride or dutasteride, double the PSA.
discriminator: Compare the adjusted value with baseline.

stem: An 82-year-old with mild dementia on donepezil has urge incontinence. She also takes diphenhydramine nightly. Her blood pressure is well controlled. Which plan is best?

options.A: Start oxybutynin; it has the least CNS effect in the class
options.B: Start tamsulosin to relax the bladder outlet instead
options.C: Start oxybutynin; donepezil will cancel its side effects
options.D: Start solifenacin and continue diphenhydramine for sleep
options.E: Stop diphenhydramine and choose mirabegron over oxybutynin

why: Antimuscarinics cause confusion in older adults, and the burden adds up across drugs such as diphenhydramine. Oxybutynin carries the highest CNS burden; cholinesterase inhibitors oppose antimuscarinics. Mirabegron, a beta3 agonist, avoids this.

whys.A: Oxybutynin has the highest CNS anticholinergic burden.
whys.B: Her problem is storage, not outlet obstruction.
whys.C: Donepezil opposes antimuscarinics; they work against each other.
whys.D: Anticholinergic burden is cumulative across her drugs.

takeaway: Dementia + urge incontinence: avoid oxybutynin, cut other anticholinergics.
discriminator: Count the whole anticholinergic load.

stem: Which description of tamoxifen's tissue actions matches the study guide?

options.A: Antagonist in breast; agonist in bone and endometrium
options.B: Antagonist in breast and endometrium; agonist in bone
options.C: Blocks aromatase in fat and other peripheral tissue
options.D: Agonist in breast; antagonist in bone and endometrium
options.E: Antagonist in every estrogen-responsive tissue

why: Tamoxifen: breast antagonist, bone and endometrium agonist. Raloxifene is endometrium-neutral.

whys.B: It is an agonist in endometrium.
whys.C: That is anastrozole and letrozole.
whys.D: The actions are reversed.

takeaway: Tamoxifen blocks in breast, stimulates in endometrium.
discriminator: Tissue decides agonist or antagonist.

stem: A 59-year-old on finasteride for 8 months reports lower libido and erectile difficulty. His urinary flow is better. Which statement is correct?

options.A: These are first-dose effects that fade within days
options.B: These are antimuscarinic effects of the drug
options.C: These mean the drug has raised his testosterone too far
options.D: These come from PDE5 inhibition and cGMP build-up
options.E: These are known effects of blocking 5-alpha-reductase

why: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors cause decreased libido and erectile dysfunction, and lower PSA by about half.

whys.A: First-dose effect belongs to alpha1 blockers.
whys.C: The drug lowers DHT.
whys.D: That is sildenafil and tadalafil.

takeaway: Finasteride: sexual side effects and a halved PSA.
discriminator: Hormonal drug, hormonal side effects.

stem: Two women take a SERM. One takes tamoxifen after breast cancer; the other takes raloxifene for osteoporosis. Which risk do both drugs share, and which belongs to only one?

options.A: Shared: endometrial cancer. Raloxifene only: VTE
options.B: Shared: VTE. Tamoxifen only: endometrial cancer
options.C: Shared: erythrocytosis. Tamoxifen only: hepatotoxicity
options.D: Shared: bone loss. Tamoxifen only: joint pain
options.E: Shared: VTE. Raloxifene only: endometrial cancer

why: Both SERMs carry increased VTE risk, similar to estrogen therapy. Tamoxifen's endometrial agonism adds endometrial hyperplasia and cancer risk; raloxifene does not.

whys.A: Raloxifene is endometrium-neutral; VTE is shared.
whys.C: Those belong to testosterone.
whys.D: Bone loss and joint pain are aromatase-inhibitor effects.

takeaway: Both clot; only tamoxifen acts on the endometrium.
discriminator: Tissue-specific agonism explains the difference.

stem: A 70-year-old stable on solifenacin starts clarithromycin. Four days later he has a very dry mouth, constipation and blurred vision. What is the mechanism?

options.A: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and raises solifenacin levels
options.B: Clarithromycin opposes solifenacin like donepezil does
options.C: Clarithromycin adds its own antimuscarinic blockade
options.D: Clarithromycin induces CYP3A4 and lowers solifenacin levels
options.E: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP2D6, as mirabegron also does

why: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin) raise solifenacin levels, so antimuscarinic effects increase.

whys.C: It is not an anticholinergic.
whys.D: Lower levels would reduce, not increase, effects.

takeaway: CYP3A4 inhibitor + solifenacin = more anticholinergic effect.
discriminator: Higher level of the same drug, not a second anticholinergic.

stem: A 38-year-old who smokes a pack a day asks for 'the regular pill' for contraception. Her mother had a pulmonary embolism at 45. Which option is most appropriate?

options.A: Raloxifene, because it avoids the endometrial cancer risk
options.B: A combined pill, because her VTE risk is only theoretical
options.C: Estradiol alone, because the dose is lower than the pill
options.D: A progestin-only method, because estrogen is contraindicated
options.E: A combined pill plus low-dose aspirin to offset clot risk

why: Estrogen raises VTE risk, more with smoking and age over 35, or a personal or family VTE history. Those factors shift a patient from candidate to contraindicated; progestin-only methods avoid estrogen.

whys.A: It is not a contraceptive and carries VTE risk itself.
whys.B: Smoking, age over 35 and family VTE history move her to contraindicated.
whys.C: It is still estrogen, and unopposed with a uterus.
whys.E: The lecture's answer is to avoid estrogen, not to offset it.

takeaway: Smoker over 35 or VTE history: no estrogen.
discriminator: Risk factors change the answer, not the dose.

stem: A 55-year-old wants an erectile dysfunction drug that does not need to be timed closely to activity. He takes no nitrates or alpha blockers. Which choice and reason match the lecture?

options.A: Tamsulosin: it treats erectile dysfunction directly
options.B: Sildenafil: longer half-life and flexible dosing
options.C: Sildenafil: it avoids the visual side effects
options.D: Tadalafil: it is the only one safe with nitrates
options.E: Tadalafil: longer half-life and flexible dosing

why: Tadalafil has a longer half-life and flexible dosing. Class adverse effects: headache, flushing, dyspepsia, visual disturbance (more notable with sildenafil).

whys.A: It is an alpha1 blocker for BPH.
whys.C: Blue-tinged vision is more notable with sildenafil.
whys.D: No PDE5 inhibitor is safe with nitrates.

takeaway: Tadalafil lasts longer.
discriminator: Same mechanism, different duration.

stem: A 22-year-old on a combined pill starts carbamazepine for a seizure disorder and St. John's wort on her own. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Both are inhibitors that raise her estrogen and clot risk
options.B: Both raise INR, so warfarin-style monitoring is needed
options.C: Both are inducers that lower contraceptive efficacy
options.D: Only carbamazepine matters; the herbal product is inert
options.E: Both block CYP2D6 and stop the pill being activated

why: Enzyme inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort) lower combined contraceptive efficacy.

whys.A: They are enzyme inducers.
whys.B: INR rises with testosterone or tamoxifen plus warfarin.
whys.D: St. John's wort is a named inducer.
whys.E: CYP2D6 inhibition is the tamoxifen issue.

takeaway: Inducers, including St. John's wort, weaken the pill.
discriminator: Induction lowers hormone levels.

stem: A 53-year-old with severe hot flashes has an intact uterus. A 55-year-old with the same symptoms had a hysterectomy. Which regimens match the lecture's rule?

options.A: An aromatase inhibitor for both, to steady estrogen levels
options.B: Tamoxifen for both, since it protects the endometrium
options.C: Estrogen alone for the first; estrogen plus progestin for the second
options.D: Estrogen alone for both, at the lowest effective dose
options.E: Estrogen plus a progestin for the first; estrogen alone for the second

why: Unopposed estrogen in a patient with a uterus significantly increases endometrial cancer risk, so a progestin is added. Without a uterus there is no endometrium to protect.

whys.A: That lowers estrogen and would worsen hot flashes.
whys.C: Unopposed estrogen with a uterus raises endometrial cancer risk.
whys.D: The uterus needs progestin protection whatever the dose.

takeaway: Uterus present: never estrogen alone.
discriminator: The progestin is there for the endometrium.

stem: A 33-year-old with PCOS and an eGFR of 28 from lupus nephritis is being considered for metformin. What is the main concern?

options.A: Hypoglycemia, as with a sulfonylurea
options.B: Common GI upset that never settles with meals
options.C: Hyperkalemia, as with spironolactone
options.D: Rare but serious lactic acidosis in renal impairment
options.E: Venous thromboembolism, as with estrogen

why: Metformin: GI upset is common and often transient; lactic acidosis is rare but serious in renal impairment, so renal dosing principles apply.

whys.A: Metformin is an insulin sensitizer.
whys.B: GI upset is common but often transient.
whys.C: That is not a metformin effect.
whys.E: That is not a metformin effect.

takeaway: Metformin and low eGFR: think lactic acidosis.
discriminator: Common and mild vs rare and serious.

stem: A 71-year-old starts tamsulosin for BPH and is scheduled for cataract surgery next month. He also takes two antihypertensives. Which pair of counseling points is correct?

options.A: Blue-tinged vision; avoid all nitrates while taking it
options.B: Libido may fall; the prostate shrinks over 6 months
options.C: Dry mouth and confusion; avoid diphenhydramine at night
options.D: First-dose dizziness on standing; tell the eye surgeon
options.E: PSA will halve; double the value at the next screening

why: Alpha1 blockers cause orthostatic hypotension and a first-dose effect, additive with antihypertensives. Floppy iris syndrome is an intraoperative complication of cataract surgery in patients on alpha1 blockers.

whys.A: Those are PDE5-inhibitor points.
whys.C: Those are antimuscarinic points.

takeaway: Tamsulosin: stand up slowly, and tell the cataract surgeon.
discriminator: Alpha1 is on vessels and the iris, not only the prostate.

stem: A man with advanced prostate cancer receives leuprolide together with bicalutamide. Which description of the pair matches the lecture?

options.A: A PDE5 inhibitor used with a nitrate
options.B: A GnRH agonist used with a receptor-level antiandrogen
options.C: An aromatase inhibitor used with a SERM
options.D: A 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor used with an alpha1 blocker
options.E: A GnRH agonist used with testosterone replacement

why: Leuprolide (a GnRH agonist) is used with antiandrogens in prostate cancer; bicalutamide is a receptor-level blocker.

whys.A: That combination is contraindicated.
whys.C: Those are breast-cancer drugs.
whys.D: That pairing is for BPH symptoms.

takeaway: Leuprolide + bicalutamide: axis plus receptor.
discriminator: Two levels of the same pathway.

stem: A man has both urgency with small frequent voids and a weak stream with hesitancy. Which pairing of drug, site and problem treated is correct?

options.A: Sildenafil: beta3 on detrusor, urgency. Tamsulosin: PDE5 at outlet, weak stream
options.B: Mirabegron: M3 block on detrusor, urgency. Tamsulosin: 5-ARI in prostate, weak stream
options.C: Oxybutynin: M3 on detrusor, weak stream. Finasteride: alpha1 at outlet, urgency
options.D: Mirabegron: beta3 on detrusor, urgency. Tamsulosin: alpha1 at outlet, weak stream
options.E: Mirabegron: alpha1 at outlet, weak stream. Tamsulosin: beta3 on detrusor, urgency

why: Mirabegron stimulates beta3 on the detrusor to relax the reservoir (storage symptoms). Tamsulosin is a uroselective alpha1 antagonist that opens the outlet (voiding symptoms).

whys.A: Sildenafil inhibits PDE5; tamsulosin blocks alpha1.
whys.B: Mirabegron is a beta3 agonist; tamsulosin is an alpha1 blocker.
whys.C: Oxybutynin treats urgency; finasteride blocks 5-alpha-reductase.

takeaway: Storage problem: detrusor drug. Voiding problem: outlet drug.
discriminator: Match the symptom to the site.

stem: A 61-year-old on warfarin for atrial fibrillation starts testosterone gel for confirmed hypogonadism. Which monitoring set is most complete for the first months?

options.A: Hematocrit, PSA and a closer watch on INR
options.B: Prolactin and a pregnancy test before each refill
options.C: Potassium and creatinine within 1 week of starting
options.D: Bone density and calcium with vitamin D levels
options.E: Hematocrit and PSA only; warfarin is unaffected

why: Testosterone therapy needs hematocrit (erythrocytosis) and PSA monitoring. Testosterone and tamoxifen raise INR with warfarin.

whys.C: That is spironolactone monitoring.
whys.D: That is aromatase-inhibitor care.

takeaway: Testosterone: hematocrit, PSA, and INR if on warfarin.
discriminator: Routine monitoring plus the interaction.

stem: A 69-year-old on amitriptyline for neuropathic pain is started on solifenacin. He becomes confused and cannot pass urine easily. Which explanation fits?

options.A: The tricyclic inhibits CYP3A4 and raises solifenacin
options.B: Additive anticholinergic burden from the two drugs
options.C: The tricyclic opposes solifenacin, as donepezil would
options.D: Solifenacin causes first-dose hypotension
options.E: Solifenacin raises blood pressure, as mirabegron can

why: Other anticholinergics (diphenhydramine, tricyclic antidepressants) add to anticholinergic burden, which is cumulative across a patient's medications.

whys.A: The inhibitors taught are ketoconazole and clarithromycin.
whys.C: Tricyclics add to the burden; donepezil opposes.
whys.D: That is the alpha1 blockers.

takeaway: Tricyclic + antimuscarinic: the burden adds up.
discriminator: Two drugs, one shared effect.

stem: A 66-year-old on letrozole for 18 months reports aching in her hands and knees. Her DXA scan shows a drop in bone density. Which plan fits the lecture?

options.A: Expected effects; add a bisphosphonate, calcium and vitamin D
options.B: Expected effects; add estradiol alone to rebuild bone
options.C: Unexpected effects; switch to tamoxifen to avoid VTE risk
options.D: Expected effects; add DMPA, which strengthens bone
options.E: Unexpected effects; check hematocrit for erythrocytosis

why: Aromatase inhibitor adverse effects are bone loss and joint pain. Bisphosphonates and calcium with vitamin D protect bone.

whys.C: Tamoxifen carries VTE risk; these effects are expected.
whys.D: DMPA causes bone density loss.

takeaway: Aromatase inhibitor: joints ache, bones thin.
discriminator: Tamoxifen spares bone; aromatase inhibitors do not.

stem: A 64-year-old on stable warfarin starts tamoxifen. Three weeks later she has nosebleeds and bruising. Which mechanism does the lecture give?

options.A: Tamoxifen raises INR with warfarin
options.B: Tamoxifen induces enzymes that clear warfarin
options.C: Tamoxifen causes erythrocytosis that thins the blood
options.D: Tamoxifen lowers INR and the bleeding is unrelated
options.E: Warfarin inhibits CYP2D6 and blocks tamoxifen activation

why: Testosterone and tamoxifen raise INR with warfarin.

whys.C: Erythrocytosis is a testosterone effect.
whys.D: The taught effect is a higher INR.
whys.E: CYP2D6 inhibitors are paroxetine and fluoxetine.

takeaway: Tamoxifen or testosterone + warfarin: INR rises.
discriminator: Check INR after adding either.
